chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id, from Yunus ibn Yaqoob, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had blood-letting performed on Monday and gave wheat to the phleotomist.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet do on Mondays regarding cupping and what did he give the practitioner?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) practice of cupping on Mondays, a day often associated with healing in Islamic tradition. It underscores the Sunnah of compensating medical practitioners, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on valuing professional services and maintaining physical well-being through prophetic methods.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-64 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Sindy, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Yunus ibn Yaqoob that he had heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say,
“God’s Prophet (MGB) had blood-letting performed on Mondays and gave wheat to the person who performed the phlebotomy on him.”
